pointers.words: If you've got gold on your hands, you might talk to Ralis, up at Kolbjorn Barrow. I've heard he wants to excavate the place.

his beloved Saarthal. Among the Skaal of Solstheim, it is said he fled to their island, and was sealed in the depths of Kolbjorn Barrow, together with the last of his relics.

But that is the tale, as it was told among the bards of Winterhold. Whatever the truth, the legend of

Ahzidal the Embittered was entombed in the depths of Kolbjorn Barrow, which has long since been buried by the ash storms. Dukaan the Dishonored was interred within White Ridge Barrow in the northwestern mountains.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: Nchardak, an ancient Dwemer city, on the eastern side of Solstheim. It's largely flooded now, but luckily the main library is still above the water.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: I'm not taking this trip for pleasure, you know. Let's get to Nchardak.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: Here we are. Nchardak. The book we're after is right inside that dome.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: I thought you were in a hurry to get to Nchardak.
The Dwemer of Nchardak appear to have been fond of these control pedestals. Luckily, I found a cube to operate it inside on my last visit.
Nchardak. The 'City of a Hundred Towers'. In its day, it was the largest of the great Dwemer Archives, and perhaps the most advanced.
These must be the "Great Workshops of Nchardak". Impressive even in ruins.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: I found their "reading room" in the ruins of Nchardak. The book is there, but it's sealed in a protective case which I wasn't able to open.
You have to go to Nchardak! That's where the thief went to! Here, let me mark it on your map.
You have to go to Nchardak! That's where the thief went to! Here, let me mark it on your map.

pointers.speaker: Remiel
pointers.words: Nchardak was actually designed to flood, you know. The Nords once tried to invade it, and the dwemer flooded it in response until they gave up.

pointers.speaker: Remiel
pointers.words: Nchardak was a powerhouse of a city, back in its prime. It created complete automatons very quickly.

pointers.speaker: Remiel
pointers.words: This is very exciting! Nchardak is considered advanced, even by Dwemeri standards!

pointers.speaker: Remiel
pointers.words: There are a couple theories about why Nchardak sank after the dwemer vanished. The most interesting is that the automatons flooded it to preserve it.

l its power coursing through my body. That fool Yassour didn't know what was coming! I'll take this back to my group at Nchardak and immediately get on a boat to Mournhold afterward. I'm sure the museum will take it off my hands for quite the coin.
Got this from a pretty excited looking Dark Elf around Raven Rock. He said it was important I got it to you as soon as I could.

pointers.speaker: Ulves Romoran
pointers.words: Well, Neloth's just going to have to wait. Varona went to Raven Rock to arrange for supplies.

pointers.speaker: Elynea Mothren
pointers.words: She left for Raven Rock hours ago. She promised to bring me back some fresh blisterwort.

pointers.speaker: Drovas Relvi
pointers.words: Neloth may be crazy, but it's better than staying in Raven Rock.
I'm sure there's plenty of people in Raven Rock to choose from.

pointers.speaker: Varona Nelas
pointers.words: I'm going to have to go to Raven Rock soon. We're running low on some things.

pointers.speaker: Ulves Romoran
pointers.words: I'd better tell Varona to bring apples and cabbage from Raven Rock.
Uh... you mean leave Raven Rock? For good? To go work for a crazed Telvanni wizard?

pointers.speaker: Ulves Romoran
pointers.words: The Raven Rock road is dangerous. I hope nothing happened to Varona.

pointers.speaker: Elynea Mothren
pointers.words: Varona goes to Raven Rock all the time. I'm sure she's fine.

pointers.speaker: Aphia Velothi
pointers.words: Those East Empire people should be ashamed of themselves for abandoning Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Tilisu Severin
pointers.words: My husband Vendil feared visitors would shun Raven Rock. I'm glad to see he was mistaken.

pointers.speaker: Tilisu Severin
pointers.words: I hope you enjoy your stay in Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Garyn Ienth
pointers.words: Welcome to Raven Rock, traveler. Could I interest you in any fine ash-grown foods?

pointers.speaker: Garyn Ienth
pointers.words: My wife and I are doing the best we can to keep Raven Rock fed.

pointers.speaker: Milore Ienth
pointers.words: My husband Garyn maintains our farm. Without him, Raven Rock would likely go hungry.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: On behalf of House Redoran and as Councilor of Raven Rock, I bid you welcome.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: Anything you can contribute to Raven Rock will be greatly appreciated... and rewarded appropriately, of course.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: Don't let the state of Raven Rock fool you. Our desire for Raven Rock's return to its former glory is as strong as the Bulwark itself.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Most exiled Dark Elves call Vvardenfell their home. I call Raven Rock our home... may it last a thousand years.

pointers.speaker: Cindiri Arano
pointers.words: You've brought Raven Rock back from the brink, traveler. I don't know how to thank you.

pointers.speaker: Cindiri Arano
pointers.words: Your efforts in Raven Rock have proven most invigorating for my husband. I haven't seen him this pleased in many years.

pointers.speaker: Cindiri Arano
pointers.words: As the wife to the Second Councilor of Raven Rock, it would be my pleasure to help you any way that I can.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: The security of both Raven Rock and Councilor Morvayn is my primary concern.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: Looking for something to lend a hand with? We have problems aplenty in Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Galdrus Hlervu
pointers.words: If they desire salvation, the citizens of Raven Rock need to open their eyes... and their pockets.

pointers.speaker: Geldis Sadri
pointers.words: I know everyone in Raven Rock, and they know me. You want stories? I've got plenty.

pointers.speaker: Dreyla Alor
pointers.words: You stuck in Raven Rock too? Horrible isn't it?
My men have laid down their lives to keep Raven Rock safe. We've fought too hard to leave. We can't just let it all go.
Raven Rock doesn't offer much in the way of companionship. You should be happy for her.
No, Councilor. He's spoken to everyone in town... twice. If House Hlaalu has a spy in Raven Rock, he's hidden beyond our means to find him.

pointers.speaker: Yrsa
pointers.words: The Dark Elves of Raven Rock keep to their city, and we Skaal keep to our village.
Councilor Morvayn is the only reason Raven Rock has survived all these years. You should pay your respects.
What brings you to Raven Rock?

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: Me? I don't care what they're called... all I know is they're a danger to Raven Rock and they need to be stopped.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: I need you to head out to Fort Frostmoth and check it out. I'm going to head back to Raven Rock and prepare the men for further assaults.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: Besides, I don't feel comfortable leaving Raven Rock behind, and I'd hate to lose any more Redoran Guard.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: They arrived here ten years ago, and have been nothing but a benefit to Raven Rock ever since.

pointers.speaker: Geldis Sadri
pointers.words: Back in 95, Vilur Ulen came to Raven Rock with a plan to take over our town.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: I need you to start out by being my eyes and ears... search Raven Rock and see if you can root out these traitors.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Without Councilor Morvayn, Raven Rock has no future. Keep that in mind next time you decide to help or not.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Raven Rock is a small settlement, so it's hard to accomplish anything in secret.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: I do. I've received some information from my sources that there could be elements of Ulen's house, House Hlaalu, already in Raven Rock.
Taproot? That's all? Add it to the Raven Rock list.
Hmm? Oh. Raven Rock. Right.
Master Neloth, I'm preparing for a trip to Raven Rock to pick up supplies.
Where is your list of things you need from Raven Rock?
Are you going to Raven Rock soon? I need something.

pointers.speaker: Varona Nelas
pointers.words: He's not here right now. I think he's in Raven Rock.
Try Raven Rock. They are in awe of me there. I'm sure almost anyone would be willing to serve me.

pointers.speaker: Edla
pointers.words: Many hunters pass through our village, and sometimes the Dark Elves of Raven Rock visit us.

pointers.speaker: Crescius Caerellius
pointers.words: But mark my words, these mines hold a secret that could put Raven Rock back on the map.

pointers.speaker: Crescius Caerellius
pointers.words: It killed my great-grandfather, and left Raven Rock with a worthless and tainted mine.
I could travel to Raven Rock and purchase some more.

pointers.speaker: Cindiri Arano
pointers.words: Adril Arano, Second Councilor of Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: When word arrived in Blacklight that the councilor's father had passed, I was asked to sail to Raven Rock with him as his second.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: I have to be. As second councilor, the security of Raven Rock is my primary concern.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: Solstheim is theoretically under my rule, but without revenue from the mine, I lack the resources to actually govern anything but Raven Rock itself.

pointers.speaker: Mirri Severin
pointers.words: That's not someone who lives in Raven Rock, I don't think... but it sounds so familiar.

pointers.speaker: Gjalund Salt-Sage
pointers.words: If it weren't for my supply runs to Raven Rock, I'd have likely sold my ship by now and moved back to Riften.

pointers.speaker: Milore Ienth
pointers.words: According to Councilor Morvayn, my husband's been Raven Rock's most important food source for decades.

pointers.speaker: Aphia Velothi
pointers.words: By the time Crescius came of age, the ebony mine in Raven Rock was shut down. He took that quite hard.

pointers.speaker: Glover Mallory
pointers.words: I wish I had a more romantic tale to tell, but I was simply seeking my fortune and chose Raven Rock to ply my trade.

pointers.speaker: Fethis Alor
pointers.words: Mark my words... the East Empire Company will return to Raven Rock, and when they do, I'll be at the top of their list.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: My doors are open if you wish to discuss matters involving Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Crescius Caerellius
pointers.words: Mark my words. Raven Rock isn't finished yet.
...might pay off my bounty this time... walk into Raven Rock a free man...

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: Then Raven Rock will no longer be attacked by those creatures.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: It's a shame. There are quite a few tales of General Carius' exploits, including the founding of Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Geldis Sadri
pointers.words: With the mines shut down, there's no telling how much longer Raven Rock's going to last. Hopefully, Councilor Morvayn has a plan.

pointers.speaker: Ralis Sedarys
pointers.words: I'll go to Raven Rock and you... you won't mention this to anyone. If you see me there, just... give a nod and I'll lend you a hand if you need it.

pointers.speaker: Ralis Sedarys
pointers.words: I'll head back to Raven Rock and round up some diggers. Once we've got something worth looking at, I'll send word to you.

pointers.speaker: Halbarn Iron-Fur
pointers.words: I have friends in Raven Rock, and a few among the Skaal. There's not much metal on the island itself, but we can find what we need, when we need it.

pointers.speaker: General Falx Carius
pointers.words: First I'll deal with you, then the soldiers in Raven Rock!

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: What you've done for me... for all of Raven Rock... goes far beyond what I would have expected from a traveler to our town.
Vendil? But he's done so much for Raven Rock... how could this be possible?

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: After everything you've already done for Raven Rock, I hate to ask for more, but I can't risk Councilor Morvayn being killed.

pointers.speaker: Crescius Caerellius
pointers.words: Our home has stood in Raven Rock since the colony was founded. Gratian helped build it with his own two hands.
Well, here we are. This is Raven Rock. Can't say I'm all that glad to see it again.
Well, here we are. Welcome to Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Gjalund Salt-Sage
pointers.words: It's an island northeast of here. Has a small Dark Elf town called Raven Rock and a handful of Nords living in Skaal Village.

pointers.speaker: Cindiri Arano
pointers.words: One of the sailors survived. Poor thing crawled all the way to Raven Rock on his hands and knees.

pointers.speaker: Captain Veleth
pointers.words: Not certain who lived there... it was already a pile of rubble when I arrived in Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Vilur Ulen wasn't the first Ulen to live in Raven Rock. His father, Valin Ulen, was one of the first Dunmer to settle here.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: I don't recognize you, so I'll assume this is your first visit to Raven Rock, outlander. State your intentions.

pointers.speaker: Rirns Llervu
pointers.words: They sprung from the ground with no warning and killed one of my companions instantly. I was so frightened, I ran all the way back to Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: With the mines open, Raven Rock has become a significant colony of the Dunmer people again.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: And with Solstheim crawling with reavers and Azura-knows what else, I can't risk any attacks on Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Neloth
pointers.words: You again. Didn't I see you in Raven Rock?

pointers.speaker: Teldryn Sero
pointers.words: I've called Raven Rock my home for a number of years. Azura knows why... it's a mess.

pointers.speaker: Teldryn Sero
pointers.words: Seems like things are looking up in Raven Rock now that the mine's open. It's a nice change.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Raven Rock started out as an Imperial settlement, but the Empire decided to abandon it just as my people were first setting foot here.

pointers.speaker: Adril Arano
pointers.words: Just remember, Raven Rock is sovereign territory of House Redoran. This is Morrowind. While you're here you will be expected to abide by our laws.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: Now, we're barely holding out here. Without the mine, Raven Rock doesn't feel like it can last much longer.

pointers.speaker: Gjalund Salt-Sage
pointers.words: It's an island northeast of here. Has a small Dark Elf town called Raven Rock and a handful of Nords living in Skaal Village.

pointers.speaker: Talvas Fathryon
pointers.words: He's off doing research in Raven Rock. I think.

pointers.speaker: Lydia
pointers.words: So this is Raven Rock, eh? Not all that much to look at.
I'd heard of the famous bulwark of Raven Rock. I believe the East Empire Company built it, or funded it.
Raven Rock... Oh, God I never thought I'd be so happy to see that name again.
Last thing I know it was in the town of Raven Rock in Solstheim in the hands of one Yassour Tansumiran.

pointers.speaker: Mathis Valen
pointers.words: I also need you to find Yassour Tansumiran in Raven Rock. He should be in possession of Wraithguard, and you need to persuade him to hand it over.
Thank you, stranger. I've found that my target boarded a ship headed straight to Raven Rock some time ago.
This man will die without proper care, so I must return to Raven Rock, but we also can't let Zirath reach whatever it is he hopes to find there.
So, the ash spawn are gone. Give Raven Rock a week before something else goes wrong.
A manor in Raven Rock. That's a step up from sleeping in the ash.
Raven Rock's barely a town compared to Whiterun, but its politics is ten times more dense. Sounds like the elves just can't live without drama.
Councilor Morvayn is the only reason Raven Rock has survived all these years. You should pay your respects.

pointers.speaker: Priest Drureth
pointers.words: The time has come for us to speed up our progress here at Raven Rock. We've been in hiding for far too long.

pointers.speaker: Serana
pointers.words: Today, I didn't stop to think if the Dunmer from Raven Rock were suffering while under mind control. All I cared about was my "vacation" here.
Raven Rock is bustling again. So many delicacies are being imported from all over Tamriel... aren't they?
Raven Rock isn't much without its mine. Serves it right.
Raven Rock has to be the most exotic place I've ever been to.

pointers.speaker: Brelyna Maryon
pointers.words: If you look far enough, you can see my home from Raven Rock.

pointers.speaker: Brelyna Maryon
pointers.words: Believe it or not, Raven Rock is one of the more diverse settlements of Morrowind.
Now that Raven Rock prospers again, perhaps the Nords will want it back. Wars will be sweet for Solstheim.
Raven Rock is a desolate town with nothing of worth to loot. We're better off finishing our business here, then sail back to Skyrim.
Now that the Raven Rock mine has reopened, coin is flowing back into the town. We'll see if that'll put Solstheim back on the Guild's map.
We Dunmer are a people of subterfuge and schemes. Raven Rock's assassination plot is but business as usual in Morrowind.
With the ebony mine reopened, Raven Rock has made itself a target to opportunists all around Tamriel. More's the opportunity for us.
One might find Raven Rock to be a desolate town, yet compared to the rest of mainland Morrowind, it is already a great city of its own.
It seems the Redoran Guards are crumbling to the Ash Spawn attacks. Raven Rock won't be the first city to be buried in ash, nor will it be the last.
Considering we just saved Raven Rock from certain destruction, the Captain should've been more generous. They make do with what they can, I suppose.
So I guessed correctly. A Nord ruin slumbers beneath Raven Rock's mine. Now, let's see if it's as horrifying as the East Empire Company believed.
Here we are... the true secret of Raven Rock's mine. The source of all the terror in this ruin.
Two elves who kidnapped a blacksmith? They're either from Raven Rock or the Thalmor - and I assure you, my people have no interest in Nord armor.
A threat to the Redoran's peace. Had it been the Ulen who ruled Raven Rock, the Redoran would've attempted the same.
I heard a lot about Raven Rock from Jenassa. It doesn't look that impressive to me.
Raven Rock used to be a rundown town. But with the mine reopened, it's become much more prosperous.
Let's hope the news of Raven Rock's recovery never reaches Hammerfell. The last thing we need is more Alik'r attention on this refuge.
It's hard to fathom that Raven Rock is one of the more prosperous towns in Morrowind. Even Riften looks better than it.
Money is flowing in Raven Rock once again, thanks to you.
Now that the mine is reopened, Raven Rock seems more lively than before.
Huh, now that business has returned to Raven Rock, so too do merchants from the mainland. Maybe I'll have a good fill at last.
The East Empire Company never keeps something useless, be it a mine, a town, or people. What happened in Raven Rock was far from irregular.
They may not sing about Raven Rock over in Skyrim... but I'll make sure your ballad is heard from Solstheim to Falkreath.

pointers.speaker: Remiel
pointers.words: If I recall from my reading, the Skaal Village is difficult to reach. Maybe we should stop by Raven Rock to rest up before we head out?
Had the Vici owned the East Empire Company in those days, they would've annexed Raven Rock already. The mine's closure may be a blessing in disguise.
For all the dirty dealings of the Vici, Raven Rock couldn't have sunken lower. With their gold, this town may see light again.
I've been wanting to visit Raven Rock, or even see those churning sands of Elsweyr. The possibilities are endless, really.

pointers.speaker: Lucien Flavius
pointers.words: Raven Rock was actually founded by the East Empire Company because of all the ebony ore here. Whatever the Dunmer say, the Empire made this place.

pointers.speaker: Lucien Flavius
pointers.words: Because of its obscure location, Raven Rock passed through the Oblivion Crisis more-or-less unscathed. One of the few places that did.

pointers.speaker: Lucien Flavius
pointers.words: Raven Rock. Nice alliterative quality. Rolls off the tongue. I approve.

pointers.words: I heard crazy old Crescius has been sneaking into Raven Rock Mine again. At his age, he's going to get himself killed in there.
Welcome to Raven Rock Mine, outlander.

Not much contact with others around here. Got the Skaal Village to the north, but the Nords there keep to themselves.
It's hard to explain, but as much as I have come to think of Skaal Village as a second home, I do still miss Skyrim.

pointers.speaker: Glover Mallory
pointers.words: If you're looking to learn more, you should head over to the Skaal Village. Someone there's bound to know more about it than I do.

pointers.speaker: Glover Mallory
pointers.words: The one Crescius "borrowed" came from the Skaal Village up north. I, uh, traded them some goods for it.

pointers.speaker: Lleril Morvayn
pointers.words: Well, there's a small enclave of Nords to the north in Skaal Village. They pretty much keep to themselves, and we both like it that way.

pointers.speaker: Hilund
pointers.words: I fight. I protect the hall. I bring in meat. And I think I could take on most of the tree lovers up in the Skaal Village.

pointers.speaker: Geldis Sadri
pointers.words: The blacksmith up at Skaal Village seems to have gone missing and they've asked us to keep an eye out.
I must take this back to Skaal Village right away.

pointers.speaker: Gjalund Salt-Sage
pointers.words: It's an island northeast of here. Has a small Dark Elf town called Raven Rock and a handful of Nords living in Skaal Village.

pointers.speaker: Storn Crag-Strider
pointers.words: As shaman of Skaal Village, I serve as both a guide and a healer, as well as a keeper of traditions.

pointers.speaker: Nikulas
pointers.words: I'm on my way to Skaal Village. Perhaps I'll see you there.

We are honored to welcome a Dragonborn to High Hrothgar.
You stand in High Hrothgar, on the slopes of Kynareth's sacred mountain.

pointers.speaker: Arngeir
pointers.words: Very few are permitted to study with us here at High Hrothgar.

pointers.speaker: Ulfric Stormcloak
pointers.words: It's good to be back in High Hrothgar after all these years.

pointers.speaker: M'aiq the Liar
pointers.words: M'aiq once walked to High Hrothgar. So many steps, he lost count.

pointers.speaker: Ulfric Stormcloak
pointers.words: You'll have to make your own decision. It's a beautiful philosophy, but outside the seclusion of High Hrothgar, I was never able to hold to it.

pointers.speaker: Ulfric Stormcloak
pointers.words: I spent almost ten years at High Hrothgar, learning the Way of the Voice. Then the Great War came... I couldn't stand missing it.
No matter. Go to High Hrothgar. Learn what the Greybeards can teach you.
High Hrothgar is a very peaceful place. Very... disconnected from the troubles of this world.

pointers.speaker: Arngeir
pointers.words: The same words were used to greet the young Talos, when he came to High Hrothgar, before he became the Emperor Tiber Septim.

pointers.speaker: Ulfric Stormcloak
pointers.words: Besides, it will be good to see High Hrothgar again.
You'd better get up to High Hrothgar immediately. There's no refusing the summons of the Greybeards. It's a tremendous honor.
Not today. I'm just not ready to make the climb to High Hrothgar. The path isn't safe.

pointers.speaker: Arch-Paladin Laracin
pointers.words: High Hrothgar is a marvel of architecture to be sure. Pity it's beauty is seldom seen elsewhere in Skyrim.
Talking peace with the Empire? Talos be my witness, they're going to backstab the Stormcloaks soon as we leave High Hrothgar.
You know the path to High Hrothgar is cold, right?

pointers.speaker: Narri
pointers.words: Looks like it's really happening. A peace council, attended by both Ulfric and Tullius, up on High Hrothgar. Maybe there's hope for Skyrim yet.

pointers.speaker: Mjoll the Lioness
pointers.words: I've been to Ivarstead a few times, but never climbed High Hrothgar. I wouldn't mind visiting the monastery at the summit.

pointers.speaker: Boti
pointers.words: You must be another pilgrim on the way up to High Hrothgar. If I were you, I'd move right through our backwards little town.

pointers.speaker: Jofthor
pointers.words: Well, if you're heading up to High Hrothgar, you'll want to watch yourself along the way. I hear wolves prowl the steps.

pointers.speaker: Wilhelm
pointers.words: So, you're headed up to High Hrothgar, aren't you?

pointers.speaker: Wilhelm
pointers.words: If you're headed up to High Hrothgar, watch your step... it's a long way down.

pointers.speaker: Klimmek
pointers.words: Hello friend. Are you passing through on your way to High Hrothgar? I'm about to make a delivery up there myself.

pointers.speaker: Barknar
pointers.words: But keep an eye out for wolves if you're headed up the path to High Hrothgar.

pointers.speaker: Birna
pointers.words: Looks like it's really happening. A peace council, attended by both Ulfric and Tullius, up on High Hrothgar. Maybe there's hope for Skyrim yet.

pointers.speaker: Serana
pointers.words: Afterwards, we can just go to High Hrothgar and deliver the horn.

pointers.speaker: Serana
pointers.words: Afterwards, we can just go to High Hrothgar and deliver the horn.
Not even the view of High Hrothgar up on the mountain? I find that hard to believe... but I'll believe nonetheless.
But now that you've gathered these "mighty lords" at High Hrothgar... Well, it would be disrespectful to the Greybeards if we just call it off, no?
I'm curious. Do the Greybeards only rely on the pilgrims to get supplies, or do they have others climb all those steps to High Hrothgar?
People who undertake pilgrimage to High Hrothgar usually pass through Ivarstead. My father once did it before I was born.
Ivarstead lies in the shadows of High Hrothgar.
The Nords hold High Hrothgar in the highest regard. It's the holiest place for many of them.
It's a pity that most Nords have little regard for High Hrothgar's doctrine of harmony.
Given High Hrothgar's height, it's a miracle that neither of us are having trouble with breathing.
I don't get the Greybeards. They could get crazy rich if they opened High Hrothgar to the pilgrims and charged them.
With High Hrothgar's importance and Ivarstead being its entrance, you'd think this town would get a lot busier.
Perhaps. Personally, I wagered they'd come to blows on the steps of High Hrothgar.

pointers.speaker: Olga
pointers.words: You must be another pilgrim on the way up to High Hrothgar. No other reason to pass through here.
If we raced to High Hrothgar from Ivarstead, who would win?
If we're here for High Hrothgar, well, you must want to rest.
Anyway! Our next destination is High Hrothgar then? Let's purchase a few apples from Carlotta and be on our way.
So, we're after a Shout. Can't say that's a particularly shocking reveal, considering the whole Dragonborn thing. Back to High Hrothgar, then?
High Hrothgar. Finally. Do I still have legs? I only ask because I can't feel them anymore.

pointers.speaker: Farkas
pointers.words: You look strong. Come to Jorrvaskr and be a Companion!

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Fight with us and you'll have stories to tell. Come up to Jorrvaskr if you're worth anything in a fight.
We need to get back to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: I've been tending to the warriors of Jorrvaskr for as long as I can remember.
Kodlak killed, Jorrvaskr attacked. How could this happen, within the walls of Whiterun?
I heard about the attack on Jorrvaskr, and the killing of your honored leader. You have my sympathies, Companion.
With respect, Companion, I'd ask that you and your friends muzzle that dog of yours. The howling coming from Jorrvaskr has gotten out of hand.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: The Companions? In Jorrvaskr? They're recruiting new members, from what I hear.
And perhaps some day, you'll join us in that battle. But for today, return to Jorrvaskr. Triumph in your victory.
We will bring the battle to their chief camp. There will be none left living to tell their stories. Only songs of Jorrvaskr will be sung.
The Silver Hand. They finally found enough courage to attack Jorrvaskr.
Those bastards will regret raising their weapons against Jorrvaskr.
Let's get back to Jorrvaskr. We'll want to pay our respects to Kodlak's spirit.

pointers.speaker: Proventus Avenicci
pointers.words: The history of Whiterun begins with Jorrvaskr, the hall of the Companions. For a long time, it was the only building on the mountain.
Be careful around the burial stones. I don't want to haul you back to Jorrvaskr on my back.
I am nobody's master, Vilkas. And last I checked, we had some empty beds in Jorrvaskr for those with a fire burning in their hearts.
That someone would attack Jorrvaskr... it's unthinkable.

pointers.speaker: Skjor
pointers.words: Here's all you need to know. Jorrvaskr is the oldest building in Whiterun. The Skyforge was here long before it was.
But you don't have to stay, if you don't want to. I'll see you back at Jorrvaskr. Stories to tell the others, eh?
The Silver Hand. They finally had the nerve to attack Jorrvaskr. We got most of them, but I think a few stragglers made it out.

pointers.speaker: Fralia Gray-Mane
pointers.words: My husband Eorlund tends the Skyforge up at Jorrvaskr, the Companions mead hall. There's no finer smith in the nine holds.

pointers.speaker: Fralia Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Now he's dead and gone and the Skyforge of Jorrvaskr lies cold.
Well, I know the Companions make their home here. Their mead hall, Jorrvaskr, is the oldest building in the city.

pointers.speaker: Adrianne Avenicci
pointers.words: But you're probably more interested in Jorrvaskr, mead hall of the Companions. Their deeds of war and valor are... legendary.

pointers.speaker: Jon Battle-Born
pointers.words: Ain't sure if they're takin' on new members, but you should talk to the Companions. They're over in their hall, Jorrvaskr.
Not for me to say. You'll have to talk to Kodlak Whitemane up in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Eorlund Gray-Mane
pointers.words: The Companions are the oldest, most honored band of warriors in Skyrim. Whiterun was built around their hall, Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Athis
pointers.words: Why would you even come to Jorrvaskr without knowing what we stand for?
Oh! Oh! Maybe Cicero will go to Jorrvaskr and dance for the Companions! They'll... Um... On second thought... maybe not.

pointers.speaker: Auri
pointers.words: The wolf strode upon great Jorrvaskr, to meet the Sons of Ysgramor. They said "what are you, but a harbinger to leave us hopeless and forlorn?"

pointers.speaker: Auri
pointers.words: And so the pack was born again as the Wolves of Jorrvaskr, to rule in life and serve in death, as the moonlight's dark hunter. Goodbye Kodlak.
Maybe not... But perhaps one day, we can journey together, like the Shield-Siblings of Jorrvaskr.
A Gray-Mane never forgets a blood debt. Those werewolf hunters took Whitemane from Jorrvaskr - vengeance is the least we must serve.
Between you and me, Uncle Vignar hated vampire jobs back when he was still fighting for Jorrvaskr. The big Nord was scared by those fangs, you see.

pointers.speaker: Olfina Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Imperial assassins will surely come for Dragonsreach. But let them try - age hasn't dulled the strength that made my uncle a legend in Jorrvaskr.
You're free to come to Jorrvaskr to have some.

pointers.speaker: Aela the Huntress
pointers.words: You'd better not get frostbite. I won't carry you back to Jorrvaskr... not this time.

pointers.speaker: Narri
pointers.words: There was an attack on Jorrvaskr in Whiterun. Kodlak Whitemane has been killed! May his soul live forever in the halls of Sovngarde.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: I've been tending to the warriors of Jorrvaskr for as long as I can remember.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: I heard about the attack on Jorrvaskr, and the killing of your honored leader. You have my sympathies, Companion.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: With respect, Companion, I'd ask that you and your friends muzzle that dog of yours. The howling coming from Jorrvaskr has gotten out of hand.

pointers.speaker: Uthgerd the Unbroken
pointers.words: Really? I don't even know what to say. You'll have to talk to Kodlak Whitemane, up in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Sure has been quiet around Jorrvaskr lately. I can only imagine Aela's anger... and suffering. We should make sure not to cross her for a while.

pointers.speaker: Lydia
pointers.words: If you want armor or weapons, go to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Serana

As Harbinger, you basically own all of Jorrvaskr's mead. Good for you, I say!
Now that you're in charge of Jorrvaskr, maybe you'll consider importing the mead from Riften?
Few creatures are as vile as the Hagravens. That they had a hand in Jorrvaskr's corruption? Their deaths are demanded.
You'll always be welcome in Jorrvaskr.
I'll mount your skull in Jorrvaskr!
For the Companions! For Jorrvaskr!
Jorrvaskr is the only sight worth beholding in Whiterun.
Dragonsreach is tall and all, but the legends are all in Jorrvaskr.
Go now, hunter, and return to Jorrvaskr a savior.
Go now, hunter, and return to Jorrvaskr a savior!
There. The greatest hunter Jorrvaskr has ever seen.
You've defeated the World-Eater and lived to tell the tale. That alone counts you among the greatest legends of Jorrvaskr.
Been thinking about the young ones in Jorrvaskr. I wonder how they'll fare without us?
Have no fear. You have Jorrvaskr's greatest huntress at your side.
You are the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr. There's nothing that you can't overcome.
If Lydia would join the Companions, I promise that no one in Jorrvaskr will make her drink if she doesn't want to.
Jorrvaskr had all the mead a woman can drink and all the company one can ask for.
Who in Jorrvaskr would want to fight alongside her after that display?
Why don't you bring the lad to Jorrvaskr sometime? We'll see if there's still an empty bed waiting for him.
An unusual task for a warrior of Jorrvaskr, wouldn't you say?
All good, all things considered. But I got to make sure Jorrvaskr is heading to a path of glory.
If there is a future that can last between us... I hope it's something beyond Jorrvaskr. Together.
Perhaps a few bottles of mead in Jorrvaskr may yet quench this guilt I feel. How we've harmed a thing of beauty just to save another.
Vignar mentioned the White Phial when we were feasting at Jorrvaskr, but I never thought it actually existed. I mean, a potion that never depletes?
Jorrvaskr's become quieter without Kodlak. Though I still feel his presence sometimes, watching over Whiterun.
Jorrvaskr's halls hold a warmth unlike any tavern. Here, every scar tells a story, and every warrior earns their place with blood and sweat.
Frea fights like each blow could be her last, yet she stands tall against the shadows. She'd fit right in at Jorrvaskr.
Jorrvaskr's warmth feels alive, while Sky Haven Temple stands cool and watchful, like a guardian waiting for the call to action.
There's Saadia, some girl that Hulda hired a few months back. Don't know her much though... We have plenty of mead at Jorrvaskr after all.
Honor is a fine trait, but for fresh faces like you, it's deeds that truly carry weight in Jorrvaskr.
Then you've misunderstood Jorrvaskr.
Jorrvaskr is the oldest building in Whiterun. It was placed here because of the Skyforge, which is even older - though no one knows by how much.
They won't. Kodlak's wisdom keeps us hidden, and we make sure not to sully Jorrvaskr's name.
To protect Skyrim, we must first protect Jorrvaskr - and that sometimes requires sacrificing those who refuse to see the greater good.
If anyone were to bring such an end to Jorrvaskr, then Skyrim would lose its protector, and all the vermin we once hunted would run free.
Trust me, you have nothing to fear here in Jorrvaskr.
Like I said, I don't know for sure. I recall some old texts in Jorrvaskr, but... Let's just continue the hunt.
But look at this - for some bandits to breach Whiterun's walls and assault Jorrvaskr, they must have planned this for months.
Oh, I... am not sure I even deserve that honor. Not when some in Jorrvaskr think I am to blame for his death, provoking the Silver Hand as I did.
I regret that you see it that way. The attack on Jorrvaskr would've happened sooner or later.
Indeed. In time, perhaps more in Jorrvaskr will see things our way, and continue our tradition.
Congratulations on becoming a bard. But just a suggestion - maybe you should take some music lessons before perfoming in Jorrvaskr.
I am truly mortified to be caught by the priestess the way we were. Let's... not speak of this when we feast at Jorrvaskr, what do you say?
Mjoll is more of a Companion than half the whelps in Jorrvaskr.
I thought you knew better than to ask, but I suppose I was mistaken. Well, let's just say Jorrvaskr would benefit from one fewer "Companion".
You have no reverence for the hunt, no respect for Jorrvaskr's spirit.
No more. By Ysgramor and Kodlak, I'll see Jorrvaskr's taint cleansed.
If you ask me, we're only inviting trouble and politics to Jorrvaskr.
But will the Huntress murder a hapless merchant? How will the world ever view the honor of Jorrvaskr again?
So... do what you must. I won't be a witness to that, but I pray... you'll come back to Jorrvaskr with your honor intact.
I will give you the benefit of the doubt. Considering what you once did for Jorrvaskr, I believe that honor still beats in your heart.
Tell me, mercenary - why follow a Companion, if you hold such disdain for Jorrvaskr?
Oh, but you are mistaken. I hold no contempt for Jorrvaskr... just for you.
Know this - there's no place for the Night Mother's servant in Jorrvaskr.
I'm leaving you. Come find me in Jorrvaskr when you've recovered your senses.
But behind that aroma... There's another familiar smell. A stench, left by the foulest creature ever known to Jorrvaskr.
He and Skjor used to be my brothers, you know. But when the time was right to kick me out of Jorrvaskr, they wouldn't even look me in the eyes.
You have no reverence for the hunt, no respect for Jorrvaskr's spirit.
I'm leaving you for good. If you know any better, you will never set foot in Jorrvaskr again.
Without it, Kodlak couldn't so easily hide the true nature of Jorrvaskr.
I should have seen this long ago. You are Sithis's pet, nothing more, nothing less - and Jorrvaskr's honor means naught to you.
I had to know why one of us betrayed Jorrvaskr's ways. Now, I've got the answer. You were never a Companion to begin with.
I've told no one else in Jorrvaskr what you've done, for I believed you'd return to us one day.
It can't be... That's Arnbjorn! The beast who betrayed Jorrvaskr and almost exposed our secret!
I don't know. That's what I hoped to find out... He was already part of the Circle when I first stepped inside Jorrvaskr.
Long as Jorrvaskr stands, Arnbjorn will never be allowed near Whiterun and its people.
Either way... he's dead now, and Jorrvaskr will continue to thrive without his stain.

pointers.speaker: Erik the Slayer
pointers.words: Thank you, Harbinger, my friend! I swear, I will not sully this name. May our fights lead us to glory! Hail to Jorrvaskr! Hail to you!
Whiterun, the home of Jorrvaskr and the Companions... These ancient stones, almost brought to ruin because of this war.
Jorrvaskr is the home of Nord warriors. I do feel that I belong here, even if I am not one of their kind.
So the Companions are secretly werewolves. That explains the smell in Jorrvaskr.
There's this stench in Jorrvaskr that it never seems to get rid of. Not sure if it's the mead or just the warriors' sweat.
The old Nord of Jorrvaskr wants his rest in Sovngarde. If it were me... I think I'd also prefer the Far Shores' peace over an eternal chase.
I've never cared much for Jorrvaskr. It's for warriors of honor, not walkers of shadows like I.
I've never cared much for Jorrvaskr. The warriors gloat over their honor, believing they can defeat anything.
Of course, so that the lot of you cowards at Jorrvaskr can frame me as "Uthgerd the Bloodthirsty", "Uthgerd the Monstrous".
Thank the gods Jorrvaskr has its own mead. The last thing Whiterun needs is the Companions starting a drunken brawl at the Bannered Mare.
Hard to imagine that not long ago, the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr was still running errands for his subordinates.
Hard to imagine that not long ago, the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr was still running errands for her subordinates.
Jorrvaskr is the mead hall of the Companions, so naturally, the Companions socialize by feasting and drinking together.
Ah. Jorrvaskr. I still recall the first time I set foot here, and the first thing they made me do was to down three bottles of mead!
I knew those dogs at Jorrvaskr would taint your purity someday. Should've just killed them all in their sleeps...
Jorrvaskr, home of the Companions. Magic is more my speed, obviously, but I can respect what they do.
I thought Jorrvaskr to be a house of heroes... But werewolves? Never in a hundred years would I imagine Skyrim's protectors to be monsters.

pointers.speaker: Kodlak Whitemane
pointers.words: Jorrvaskr's warriors should always be united by both hardship and strong words.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: Harbinger, hmm? Jorrvaskr is in capable hands. I suppose I should offer congratulations... though I'll keep teasing you about your muddy boots.
Remember, loyalty runs both ways in Jorrvaskr.
I never reached the ranks of the Circle - not that I ever cared for it. Regardless, I knew Jorrvaskr still forged true warriors. You prove it.

pointers.speaker: Torvar
pointers.words: A toast to Jorrvaskr's mead - stronger than half the Nords who drink it!
Still, the people of Whiterun look to Jorrvaskr for answers, don't they?
Jorrvaskr will answer the call even so. Still, we stir neither for rumors nor doubts.
The Whitewatch Tower has fallen. The people already look at Jorrvaskr with questions in their eyes.
Wolves are scaring the livestock again. The farmers beg for us in Jorrvaskr to hunt them.

pointers.speaker: Aela the Huntress
pointers.words: Well done. You've brought pride to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Brill
pointers.words: Skjor's gone? Damn it all... I'll miss him, even if he never missed a chance to growl at me. Jorrvaskr won't be the same without him.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: You've returned! Jorrvaskr has been too quiet without you bustling about.

pointers.speaker: Vignar Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Bah! True. Call it wishful thinking from an old man who's enjoyed the company in that hall for many years... I'll respect the autonomy of Jorrvaskr.
I don't want to haul you back to Jorrvaskr on my back.
Was Jorrvaskr a ship once? Must've been. And I'm upstream without a paddle.
Well, I know the Companions make their home here. Their mead hall, Jorrvaskr, is the oldest building in the city.
We're actually joining the Companions of Jorrvaskr? How tremendously macho! They'll never believe me back home.
Axe fragment recovered! Let's head on back to Jorrvaskr and watch them all fawn over it.
I have to admit, I didn't see that one coming. It's not like we spend that much time in Jorrvaskr, after all.

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Jorrvaskr really feels like home now.

pointers.speaker: Aela the Huntress
pointers.words: Kodlak? You'll most likely find him in his quarters in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Farkas
pointers.words: Have you checked his quarters in Jorrvaskr? It's downstairs, at the end of the hall.

pointers.speaker: Farkas
pointers.words: You look strong. Come to Jorrvaskr and be a Companion!

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Fight with us and you'll have stories to tell. Come up to Jorrvaskr if you're worth anything in a fight.
We need to get back to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: I've been tending to the warriors of Jorrvaskr for as long as I can remember.
Kodlak killed, Jorrvaskr attacked. How could this happen, within the walls of Whiterun?
I heard about the attack on Jorrvaskr, and the killing of your honored leader. You have my sympathies, Companion.
With respect, Companion, I'd ask that you and your friends muzzle that dog of yours. The howling coming from Jorrvaskr has gotten out of hand.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: The Companions? In Jorrvaskr? They're recruiting new members, from what I hear.
And perhaps some day, you'll join us in that battle. But for today, return to Jorrvaskr. Triumph in your victory.
We will bring the battle to their chief camp. There will be none left living to tell their stories. Only songs of Jorrvaskr will be sung.
The Silver Hand. They finally found enough courage to attack Jorrvaskr.
Those bastards will regret raising their weapons against Jorrvaskr.
Let's get back to Jorrvaskr. We'll want to pay our respects to Kodlak's spirit.

pointers.speaker: Proventus Avenicci
pointers.words: The history of Whiterun begins with Jorrvaskr, the hall of the Companions. For a long time, it was the only building on the mountain.
Be careful around the burial stones. I don't want to haul you back to Jorrvaskr on my back.
I am nobody's master, Vilkas. And last I checked, we had some empty beds in Jorrvaskr for those with a fire burning in their hearts.
That someone would attack Jorrvaskr... it's unthinkable.

pointers.speaker: Skjor
pointers.words: Here's all you need to know. Jorrvaskr is the oldest building in Whiterun. The Skyforge was here long before it was.
But you don't have to stay, if you don't want to. I'll see you back at Jorrvaskr. Stories to tell the others, eh?
The Silver Hand. They finally had the nerve to attack Jorrvaskr. We got most of them, but I think a few stragglers made it out.

pointers.speaker: Fralia Gray-Mane
pointers.words: My husband Eorlund tends the Skyforge up at Jorrvaskr, the Companions mead hall. There's no finer smith in the nine holds.

pointers.speaker: Fralia Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Now he's dead and gone and the Skyforge of Jorrvaskr lies cold.
Well, I know the Companions make their home here. Their mead hall, Jorrvaskr, is the oldest building in the city.

pointers.speaker: Adrianne Avenicci
pointers.words: But you're probably more interested in Jorrvaskr, mead hall of the Companions. Their deeds of war and valor are... legendary.

pointers.speaker: Jon Battle-Born
pointers.words: Ain't sure if they're takin' on new members, but you should talk to the Companions. They're over in their hall, Jorrvaskr.
Not for me to say. You'll have to talk to Kodlak Whitemane up in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Eorlund Gray-Mane
pointers.words: The Companions are the oldest, most honored band of warriors in Skyrim. Whiterun was built around their hall, Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Athis
pointers.words: Why would you even come to Jorrvaskr without knowing what we stand for?
Oh! Oh! Maybe Cicero will go to Jorrvaskr and dance for the Companions! They'll... Um... On second thought... maybe not.

pointers.speaker: Auri
pointers.words: The wolf strode upon great Jorrvaskr, to meet the Sons of Ysgramor. They said "what are you, but a harbinger to leave us hopeless and forlorn?"

pointers.speaker: Auri
pointers.words: And so the pack was born again as the Wolves of Jorrvaskr, to rule in life and serve in death, as the moonlight's dark hunter. Goodbye Kodlak.
Maybe not... But perhaps one day, we can journey together, like the Shield-Siblings of Jorrvaskr.
A Gray-Mane never forgets a blood debt. Those werewolf hunters took Whitemane from Jorrvaskr - vengeance is the least we must serve.
Between you and me, Uncle Vignar hated vampire jobs back when he was still fighting for Jorrvaskr. The big Nord was scared by those fangs, you see.

pointers.speaker: Olfina Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Imperial assassins will surely come for Dragonsreach. But let them try - age hasn't dulled the strength that made my uncle a legend in Jorrvaskr.
You're free to come to Jorrvaskr to have some.

pointers.speaker: Aela the Huntress
pointers.words: You'd better not get frostbite. I won't carry you back to Jorrvaskr... not this time.

pointers.speaker: Narri
pointers.words: There was an attack on Jorrvaskr in Whiterun. Kodlak Whitemane has been killed! May his soul live forever in the halls of Sovngarde.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: I've been tending to the warriors of Jorrvaskr for as long as I can remember.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: I heard about the attack on Jorrvaskr, and the killing of your honored leader. You have my sympathies, Companion.

pointers.speaker: Hulda
pointers.words: With respect, Companion, I'd ask that you and your friends muzzle that dog of yours. The howling coming from Jorrvaskr has gotten out of hand.

pointers.speaker: Uthgerd the Unbroken
pointers.words: Really? I don't even know what to say. You'll have to talk to Kodlak Whitemane, up in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Sure has been quiet around Jorrvaskr lately. I can only imagine Aela's anger... and suffering. We should make sure not to cross her for a while.

pointers.speaker: Lydia
pointers.words: If you want armor or weapons, go to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Serana
pointers.words: The mercenaries from Jorrvaskr? They're still around?
Jorrvaskr seems tempting enough to adventurers all around. But it'd be even better if it offers Black-Briar Mead instead of the local mead.
As Harbinger, you basically own all of Jorrvaskr's mead. Good for you, I say!
Now that you're in charge of Jorrvaskr, maybe you'll consider importing the mead from Riften?
Few creatures are as vile as the Hagravens. That they had a hand in Jorrvaskr's corruption? Their deaths are demanded.
You'll always be welcome in Jorrvaskr.
I'll mount your skull in Jorrvaskr!
For the Companions! For Jorrvaskr!
Jorrvaskr is the only sight worth beholding in Whiterun.
Dragonsreach is tall and all, but the legends are all in Jorrvaskr.
Go now, hunter, and return to Jorrvaskr a savior.
Go now, hunter, and return to Jorrvaskr a savior!
There. The greatest hunter Jorrvaskr has ever seen.
You've defeated the World-Eater and lived to tell the tale. That alone counts you among the greatest legends of Jorrvaskr.
Been thinking about the young ones in Jorrvaskr. I wonder how they'll fare without us?
Have no fear. You have Jorrvaskr's greatest huntress at your side.
You are the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr. There's nothing that you can't overcome.
If Lydia would join the Companions, I promise that no one in Jorrvaskr will make her drink if she doesn't want to.
Jorrvaskr had all the mead a woman can drink and all the company one can ask for.
Who in Jorrvaskr would want to fight alongside her after that display?
Why don't you bring the lad to Jorrvaskr sometime? We'll see if there's still an empty bed waiting for him.
An unusual task for a warrior of Jorrvaskr, wouldn't you say?
All good, all things considered. But I got to make sure Jorrvaskr is heading to a path of glory.
If there is a future that can last between us... I hope it's something beyond Jorrvaskr. Together.
Perhaps a few bottles of mead in Jorrvaskr may yet quench this guilt I feel. How we've harmed a thing of beauty just to save another.
Vignar mentioned the White Phial when we were feasting at Jorrvaskr, but I never thought it actually existed. I mean, a potion that never depletes?
Jorrvaskr's become quieter without Kodlak. Though I still feel his presence sometimes, watching over Whiterun.
Jorrvaskr's halls hold a warmth unlike any tavern. Here, every scar tells a story, and every warrior earns their place with blood and sweat.
Frea fights like each blow could be her last, yet she stands tall against the shadows. She'd fit right in at Jorrvaskr.
Jorrvaskr's warmth feels alive, while Sky Haven Temple stands cool and watchful, like a guardian waiting for the call to action.
There's Saadia, some girl that Hulda hired a few months back. Don't know her much though... We have plenty of mead at Jorrvaskr after all.
Honor is a fine trait, but for fresh faces like you, it's deeds that truly carry weight in Jorrvaskr.
Then you've misunderstood Jorrvaskr.
Jorrvaskr is the oldest building in Whiterun. It was placed here because of the Skyforge, which is even older - though no one knows by how much.
They won't. Kodlak's wisdom keeps us hidden, and we make sure not to sully Jorrvaskr's name.
To protect Skyrim, we must first protect Jorrvaskr - and that sometimes requires sacrificing those who refuse to see the greater good.
If anyone were to bring such an end to Jorrvaskr, then Skyrim would lose its protector, and all the vermin we once hunted would run free.
Trust me, you have nothing to fear here in Jorrvaskr.
Like I said, I don't know for sure. I recall some old texts in Jorrvaskr, but... Let's just continue the hunt.
But look at this - for some bandits to breach Whiterun's walls and assault Jorrvaskr, they must have planned this for months.
Oh, I... am not sure I even deserve that honor. Not when some in Jorrvaskr think I am to blame for his death, provoking the Silver Hand as I did.
I regret that you see it that way. The attack on Jorrvaskr would've happened sooner or later.
Indeed. In time, perhaps more in Jorrvaskr will see things our way, and continue our tradition.
Congratulations on becoming a bard. But just a suggestion - maybe you should take some music lessons before perfoming in Jorrvaskr.
I am truly mortified to be caught by the priestess the way we were. Let's... not speak of this when we feast at Jorrvaskr, what do you say?
Mjoll is more of a Companion than half the whelps in Jorrvaskr.
I thought you knew better than to ask, but I suppose I was mistaken. Well, let's just say Jorrvaskr would benefit from one fewer "Companion".
You have no reverence for the hunt, no respect for Jorrvaskr's spirit.
No more. By Ysgramor and Kodlak, I'll see Jorrvaskr's taint cleansed.
If you ask me, we're only inviting trouble and politics to Jorrvaskr.
But will the Huntress murder a hapless merchant? How will the world ever view the honor of Jorrvaskr again?
So... do what you must. I won't be a witness to that, but I pray... you'll come back to Jorrvaskr with your honor intact.
I will give you the benefit of the doubt. Considering what you once did for Jorrvaskr, I believe that honor still beats in your heart.
Tell me, mercenary - why follow a Companion, if you hold such disdain for Jorrvaskr?
Oh, but you are mistaken. I hold no contempt for Jorrvaskr... just for you.
Know this - there's no place for the Night Mother's servant in Jorrvaskr.
I'm leaving you. Come find me in Jorrvaskr when you've recovered your senses.
But behind that aroma... There's another familiar smell. A stench, left by the foulest creature ever known to Jorrvaskr.
He and Skjor used to be my brothers, you know. But when the time was right to kick me out of Jorrvaskr, they wouldn't even look me in the eyes.
You have no reverence for the hunt, no respect for Jorrvaskr's spirit.
I'm leaving you for good. If you know any better, you will never set foot in Jorrvaskr again.
Without it, Kodlak couldn't so easily hide the true nature of Jorrvaskr.
I should have seen this long ago. You are Sithis's pet, nothing more, nothing less - and Jorrvaskr's honor means naught to you.
I had to know why one of us betrayed Jorrvaskr's ways. Now, I've got the answer. You were never a Companion to begin with.
I've told no one else in Jorrvaskr what you've done, for I believed you'd return to us one day.
It can't be... That's Arnbjorn! The beast who betrayed Jorrvaskr and almost exposed our secret!
I don't know. That's what I hoped to find out... He was already part of the Circle when I first stepped inside Jorrvaskr.
Long as Jorrvaskr stands, Arnbjorn will never be allowed near Whiterun and its people.
Either way... he's dead now, and Jorrvaskr will continue to thrive without his stain.

pointers.speaker: Erik the Slayer
pointers.words: Thank you, Harbinger, my friend! I swear, I will not sully this name. May our fights lead us to glory! Hail to Jorrvaskr! Hail to you!
Whiterun, the home of Jorrvaskr and the Companions... These ancient stones, almost brought to ruin because of this war.
Jorrvaskr is the home of Nord warriors. I do feel that I belong here, even if I am not one of their kind.
So the Companions are secretly werewolves. That explains the smell in Jorrvaskr.
There's this stench in Jorrvaskr that it never seems to get rid of. Not sure if it's the mead or just the warriors' sweat.
The old Nord of Jorrvaskr wants his rest in Sovngarde. If it were me... I think I'd also prefer the Far Shores' peace over an eternal chase.
I've never cared much for Jorrvaskr. It's for warriors of honor, not walkers of shadows like I.
I've never cared much for Jorrvaskr. The warriors gloat over their honor, believing they can defeat anything.
Of course, so that the lot of you cowards at Jorrvaskr can frame me as "Uthgerd the Bloodthirsty", "Uthgerd the Monstrous".
Thank the gods Jorrvaskr has its own mead. The last thing Whiterun needs is the Companions starting a drunken brawl at the Bannered Mare.
Hard to imagine that not long ago, the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr was still running errands for his subordinates.
Hard to imagine that not long ago, the Harbinger of Jorrvaskr was still running errands for her subordinates.
Jorrvaskr is the mead hall of the Companions, so naturally, the Companions socialize by feasting and drinking together.
Ah. Jorrvaskr. I still recall the first time I set foot here, and the first thing they made me do was to down three bottles of mead!
I knew those dogs at Jorrvaskr would taint your purity someday. Should've just killed them all in their sleeps...
Jorrvaskr, home of the Companions. Magic is more my speed, obviously, but I can respect what they do.
I thought Jorrvaskr to be a house of heroes... But werewolves? Never in a hundred years would I imagine Skyrim's protectors to be monsters.

pointers.speaker: Kodlak Whitemane
pointers.words: Jorrvaskr's warriors should always be united by both hardship and strong words.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: Harbinger, hmm? Jorrvaskr is in capable hands. I suppose I should offer congratulations... though I'll keep teasing you about your muddy boots.
Remember, loyalty runs both ways in Jorrvaskr.
I never reached the ranks of the Circle - not that I ever cared for it. Regardless, I knew Jorrvaskr still forged true warriors. You prove it.

pointers.speaker: Torvar
pointers.words: A toast to Jorrvaskr's mead - stronger than half the Nords who drink it!
Still, the people of Whiterun look to Jorrvaskr for answers, don't they?
Jorrvaskr will answer the call even so. Still, we stir neither for rumors nor doubts.
The Whitewatch Tower has fallen. The people already look at Jorrvaskr with questions in their eyes.
Wolves are scaring the livestock again. The farmers beg for us in Jorrvaskr to hunt them.

pointers.speaker: Aela the Huntress
pointers.words: Well done. You've brought pride to Jorrvaskr.

pointers.speaker: Brill
pointers.words: Skjor's gone? Damn it all... I'll miss him, even if he never missed a chance to growl at me. Jorrvaskr won't be the same without him.

pointers.speaker: Tilma the Haggard
pointers.words: You've returned! Jorrvaskr has been too quiet without you bustling about.

pointers.speaker: Vignar Gray-Mane
pointers.words: Bah! True. Call it wishful thinking from an old man who's enjoyed the company in that hall for many years... I'll respect the autonomy of Jorrvaskr.
I don't want to haul you back to Jorrvaskr on my back.
Was Jorrvaskr a ship once? Must've been. And I'm upstream without a paddle.
Well, I know the Companions make their home here. Their mead hall, Jorrvaskr, is the oldest building in the city.
We're actually joining the Companions of Jorrvaskr? How tremendously macho! They'll never believe me back home.
Axe fragment recovered! Let's head on back to Jorrvaskr and watch them all fawn over it.
I have to admit, I didn't see that one coming. It's not like we spend that much time in Jorrvaskr, after all.

pointers.speaker: Ria
pointers.words: Jorrvaskr really feels like home now.

pointers.words: Kodlak? You'll most likely find him in his quarters in Jorrvaskr.

pointers.words: Have you checked his quarters in Jorrvaskr? It's downstairs, at the end of the hall.

er, named Greorg, came by. He applauded me for my effort. As reward, he told me about some treasure at the old ruins of Rannveig's Fast a little north from here. He was going there with his hunting friends this evening and told me to wait for him here at the well, so we could all

pointers.speaker: Delphine
pointers.words: Lucan at the Riverwood Trader had his store broken into the other night. Oddly enough, barely anything's been stolen.
Changed your mind? Come with me. I'm heading to Riverwood. It's just up the road and my uncle Alvor is the blacksmith there.

pointers.speaker: Delphine
pointers.words: I'll see you back in Riverwood.
A sale? To attract new customers? Camilla, everyone in Riverwood already shops here. There are no more customers.
Be glad you're here in the city, and not out in Riverwood. Those poor sods don't even have a wall.
Come on. I'll feel better once we're under cover in Riverwood.

pointers.words: Well, I suppose it's back to the Shivering Isles. The trouble Haskill can get into while I'm gone simply boggles the mind...

pointers.speaker: Staada
pointers.words: My name is Staada, of the Aureals. I am a guardian of the Shivering Isles, and the favored servant of the Prince of Madness.
pointers.from: Skyrim Extended Cut - Saints and Seducers.esp

pointers.speaker: Staada
pointers.words: Look around you. The Shivering Isles have already touched your realm, and the consequences are obvious. Our worlds belong apart.

pointers.from: Skyrim Extended Cut - Saints and Seducers.esp

pointers.words: This is the Shivering Isles. The two halves of the realm are as divided as Lord Sheogorath himself. The climate here is no less unpredictable.

pointers.words: What you see is not real... Not even this place, to be honest. As you have just known, I become Sheogorath when I went the Shivering Isles. However I was the "Gentleman With a Cane" when I returned back to Cyrodiil.

pointers.speaker: Sheogorath
pointers.words: Oh... Ok, ok... Calm down! I get off but just a moment, right? You said that, well I said that, actually. No? Damn... I'll go back in the Shivering Isles meanwhile. I'll slap Haskill in the face because he opened the door.

pointers.speaker: Sheogorath

pointers.speaker: Sheogorath
pointers.words: Farewell? "Farewell" is a word for mortals, not for you! Uh? I'm listening a voice in me. He's me. In the Shivering Isles, actually. The voice is saying: "See you again, Dragonborn. May Nocturnal guides you." Ha ha ha ha ha!

I have to warn you, this staff makes me Lord of the Shivering Isles, so you know... I'm kind of a big deal...
This place is bizarre. It's like part of the Shivering Isles is leaking through into Mundus. I can't imagine that's a good thing.
Go back to the Shivering Isles!
